title: The Midterms Have Changed the AI Narrative: S&P Down 4.4%, Nasdaq Down 5.5% | The Weekly Wrap

metadata.title: The Midterms Have Changed the AI Narrative: S&P Down 4.4%, Nasdaq Down 5.5% | The Weekly Wrap

summary: Eisman links the midterm outcome and a sharp AI selloff to potential construction restrictions. He contrasts fragile neocloud financing with diversified hyperscalers, reviews Anthropic growth and compute efficiency, and surveys company results. His core distinction is that strong equipment orders establish current capex, not eventual AI returns. The verified Anthropic slowdown and Alphabet cash-flow deterioration support caution, but neither establishes token-maxing causality or the demise of traditional search.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman delivers a solo monologue; inserted advertisements and opening montage are excluded.
framework_points: Compare fixed-income constraints with equity narratives.
Separate current supplier demand from ultimate AI economics.
Look through earnings beats to guidance, pricing power and cash flow.
tools_and_charts: Anthropic quarterly revenue and revenue/compute ratio
transcript_cautions: Recording date is explicitly November 5, though weekly wrap is dated November 6.
Captions alternate nVent and Enphase in the stock list; exact ticker attribution is uncertain.
The caption omits one Anthropic sequential growth number and gives slightly inaccurate earlier growth percentages.

claims.claim: AI spending has pushed Google quarterly free cash flow to about negative $9 billion and Amazon to negative $33 billion.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Verify Amazon same-quarter cash-flow reconciliation and both companies' annual figures.
claims.reason: Alphabet negative $9.065 billion quarterly FCF is verified; Amazon's figure has not been independently inspected in this review.

evidence.title: Alphabet Q3 2026 Earnings Release
evidence.finding: Quarterly operating cash flow $42.290 billion less capex $51.355 billion gives negative $9.065 billion FCF; trailing-year FCF remains positive $19.747 billion. Search query growth is described as the fastest in five years.

claims.next_check: Verify Amazon same-quarter cash-flow reconciliation and both companies' annual figures.

claims.claim: Slower search revenue growth signals replacement of Google's high-moat search by capital-intensive, low-switching-cost AI.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Analyze query mix, paid clicks, monetization, AI incremental costs and search market share.
claims.reason: Alphabet reports strong query growth. A slower revenue growth rate alone cannot identify substitution, cannibalization or lasting moat erosion.

claims.claim: Anthropic Q3 sequential revenue growth slowed to about 47%, while revenue divided by compute expense fell from 2.08 to 1.72.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Recompute from Q2 and Q3 revenue and compute expense in the S-1/A.
claims.qualifications: The transcript's earlier 2026 growth percentages are approximate and partly omitted; the verified Q2 growth is 144.24%, not 147%.
claims.reason: Inspected primary evidence supports this narrowly stated claim.

evidence.title: Anthropic Form S-1/A, Amendment 2
evidence.finding: Quarterly table reports Q2/Q3 revenue $11.555/$16.956 billion and compute expense $5.558/$9.863 billion. Sequential revenue growth slowed to 46.74%; revenue/compute fell from 2.079 to 1.719.

claims.next_check: Recompute from Q2 and Q3 revenue and compute expense in the S-1/A.
